name: Paul
description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament

points: They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: Saul was consenting unto Stephen's death. This is Saul who becomes Paul, part of the same people persecuting the church, killing disciples and women, thinking he was doing it for the right reasons. That is why the scripture says judge no one before their time; a man as evil as Saul was doing back there became Paul the apostle.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: “Saul was consenting unto his death.” In the time of Stephen’s death, Saul, who became Paul, consented, and “there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.” The twelve apostles remained in Jerusalem, but their disciples, the deacons, were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: “And Saul was consenting unto his death”: Stephen’s death. At this time Saul was the enemy of the church; he agreed to Stephen’s stoning.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: As for Saul, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, haling men and women and committing them to prison. This is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again; they will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Saul is still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, going to the high priest for letters to Damascus so he can bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and drag them bound to Jerusalem. This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying, because when they notice you by your last name or your fringes you will be persecuted.
Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed.

Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly.

Ananias was sent that Saul might receive his sight “and be filled with the Holy Ghost”, just like Stephen was. Not filled with the holy opinions, the holy mistakes or the holy errors: filled with the Holy Ghost.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.

Saul increased in strength and confounded the Jews: that is why the bishop says read four chapters a day. We have to increase our strength in the scriptures to confound those that challenge us, not sit down and do debates.

All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
“And Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.” Saul is the one who later became Paul. They went to the same schools of learning.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work. When Bishop says separate that brother for the work, he's not talking about Atlanta, Miami, or California. Did Israel only scatter in America? Separate them for the work means no matter where the work is, you got to go there.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: The Jews were contradicting everything. The kingdom of Judah was going against the understanding that Paul brought about Christ. It wasn't all the kingdom of Judah; it was these certain scribes and Pharisees.
Paul and Barnabas waxed bold: it was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you, Judah; but seeing ye put it from you, lo, we turn to the Gentiles. Who are these Gentiles?
Notice what I want you to see out of that verse: it was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you. Who is Paul talking to? He's talking to the kingdom of Judah.
Paul said, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify mine office, meaning he's going to make it crystal clear who he's an apostle to: what's his mission, what's his goal.
Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold. They waxed bold. Why were they waxing bold? Because they had the spirit of Christ inside of them.

And said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles. So Paul and Barnabas had a clear understanding of the word of God, a clear understanding of the prophecy of Zechariah 12:7, that said that the gospel would come to the southern kingdom, or the Jews, first. But since some of them rejected it, the religious leaders at the time, now the gospel is being brought to the Gentiles, which is the northern kingdom according to the Bible.

“But seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.” When you say these Gentiles are heathens, you are saying Paul and them went to teach the white man, the African, the Arab and the Filipino. No: they went to the northern kingdom scattered abroad, the Gentiles dispersed among the nations, and to the dispersed of Judah.

In almost twenty years of teaching, I have noticed that America is the land of privilege, and our people here carry a certain entitlement: I heard that already, Bible, Israelite, whatever. Go out to Africa or the islands where our people are poor, and they listen, because poverty opens your ears quickly. In Zambia I saw a house of all brick with a tin roof and no windows, and kids running out of it playing barefoot, families growing crops and selling them to eat. They listen. But here, even in the ghetto with running water and a toilet, still entitled. That is why we get a heavier reception outside of the States. It is the same pattern as Paul: rejected at Jerusalem, received among the scattered.

But the Jews stirred up the devout and honourable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their coasts. Paul and Barnabas got deported out of the land because of their own people.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: Then certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium persuaded the people, and having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead. They knocked Paul upside the head with stones, and he went to the third heavens: that is the vision he spoke of in 2 Corinthians 12.
It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul: men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work. So Paul said, we should not take him; he departed from us and did not come with us to the work.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Muhammad said an angel came and gave him the revelation of the Quran. Remember the scripture said we sacrificed unto devils. Now watch: a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying. She was a witch; the same way Balaam had the spirit of divination and could see things in the future, this woman had a devil on her and could see things. The demon in her followed Paul and cried, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation. The demons in her knew who they were.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: How did she know Paul was a servant of the most high God? She had the spirit of divination; she could look at you and read the spirit within you. Paul rebuked the spirit because he knew according to the laws of God that the spirit within her was not right: a familiar spirit, a demon within her giving her that ability to give a word of knowledge, as you say it in church.

Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her; and he came out the same hour. What did Paul rebuke? The spirit. There are evil spirits that have these kinds of powers, to certain limits. Muhammad claimed to have revelations; I would not be surprised if evil spirits were dealing with him. Not just the white man has the spirit of a devil. Remember the scripture: if an angel or anybody tells you anything different, do not listen, because it could be the Lord proving you; and if they tell you something and it comes to pass, still do not follow them, because the Lord is proving you to see whether you will trust in him or in that devil.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Customs which are not lawful for us to receive: what Paul and them were teaching was the laws of God. Wherever Paul and Barnabas and Silas and the other apostles went, they taught the laws of God in the name of Christ, and the Romans said we ain't supposed to be following the Bible laws. They were commanded to be beaten for teaching in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ the laws, statutes and commandments.
And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God, and the prisoners heard them.

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

points: Look at the proximity of Thessalonica and Berea on the map; Paul was moving through Greece and we have to familiarize ourselves with these names.
The Jews of Thessalonica followed Paul to Berea to stir up the people, the same way people follow us around: they know if this doctrine spreads it is over for them.
Be ready to travel, as the bishop says; when Paul reached Athens he needed men with him to help him teach.
Seek the Lord: return to God through believing on his son Jesus Christ; that is what Paul was teaching in Athens.

After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth. So what do we see? We see the church of Corinth being corrected for the sins that they are in. Remember this, Paul is not going to them saying, hey, I am in the midst of all of these sins and I need y'all's help. It is actually the other way around. They are in the midst of all kinds of sins in the church of Corinth. Paul is there correcting them. Do not do this, do not do that. Here is the law. Do not muzzle the ox. Giving them the laws in various areas. And they are like, I want to put hands on him. For doing what? For correcting them with the word of God, for showing them the revelation of Christ, showing that the sacrifice was only a representation of the real sacrifice that was going to come, that walked amongst them in their time.
Aquila and Priscilla left Rome, met Paul in Corinth, travelled with him and taught Apollos the way of God more perfectly.

note.label: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

points: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace. So why was Paul dealing with the Corinthians so boldly? Why does he say be not afraid? What were the Corinthians threatening to do? So the Lord had to come to Paul and say, listen, you have got to make your face harder than their face, make your forehead stronger than their forehead, because they are going to try to sway you and intimidate you from teaching the gospel of Christ. And hold not thy peace, meaning do not spare. That is why Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13, if I come unto you again I am not going to spare. Because the Lord said, do not hold your peace, do not hold back. Because the Lord knew the Corinthians were wicked.

Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace. The Lord came to Paul in a vision and strengthened him. There are many times when you travel to these places, and due to the influx of a certain religion or the heathen, you'll feel that spirit of being discouraged, thinking the mission won't prosper. But that's not why the Lord sent you there. The Lord had you go there to do as he commanded you to do.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: Paul, having passed through the upper coasts, came to Ephesus. Look at the map and see how close Ephesus is to Colosse.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

points: God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul.

These were a chief priest's sons, practicing exorcisms because they were delving in the black arts. Jesus I know and Paul I know proves that the spirits know those sons and daughters of the Most High who are diligent in this truth, who have repented of their sins and are doing the work of the most high God.

Not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people. Turned them away from idolatry to serving the one true God and believing on Jesus the Christ.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

points: Notice what it says: “this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands”. The much people, brothers and sisters, included the women.

This is why, when they came into the church of Corinth, Paul said let the women keep silence in the churches: they came from worshipping Diana, where they said women rule, women power. The women came in saying, brothers, what’s wrong with the women leading us? They did it when we was in Ephesus. Paul said shut the hell up over there with that, this is all out of order, don’t bring that up in here. That’s how they sound on clubhouse today; same thing.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: When the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow: so, they came together on the first day of the week to break bread because Paul was leaving. Key point, Paul was about to leave, and they were just breaking bread, sending him off. That's greetings, like, I'mma send you on your way. I pray that you be in good health. Godspeed on your way. So, they came together and they ate.
Paul authored most of the New Testament. Let's see how Paul felt about the feast of Pentecost.

For he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost: Paul did everything in his power to keep the law we read about in Exodus 23 and Deuteronomy 16, to be in Jerusalem for the feast of Pentecost.

So why does a Christian in 2026 think Colossians 2 and 16 is telling us we don't have to celebrate the feast of Pentecost? Didn't Paul write the book of Colossians? Was Paul confused? Surely Paul's not confused. Surely the fake Christian in 2026 is confused.
The chief captain asked Paul, art not thou that Egyptian? Joseph, Moses and Paul all passed for Egyptians.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

points: “I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia”: Cilicia is Turkey. “A citizen of no mean city”: a citizen of no ghetto. Paul was not raised or born in a ghetto.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: So although Paul had Roman citizenship, he was still an Israelite, a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin. This is what Christians do not understand.
Paul said, is it lawful for you to scourge a man that's a Roman? Take heed what you do to Paul, for he is a Roman.
He said yea, meaning he had Roman citizenship, because Romans 11:1 tells you that Paul was of the tribe of Benjamin, of the nation of Israel.

Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people: so Paul repented of that, because he didn't know he was the high priest. During this time, it was not lawful, but they did it anyway: they had two high priests. Paul probably knew about the other high priest.

I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: Paul confessed he was the son of a Pharisee, a Benjamite from the tribe of Benjamin. He noticed that the crowd was Pharisees and Sadducees, so he took advantage of that and said, hey, I'm a Pharisee, and that's what caused a split amongst the council.
The Pharisees and Sadducees make up three tribes: Judah, Benjamin and Levi. Paul was a Benjamite, but he was a Pharisee. But the high priest only and always was of the tribe of Levi.
“He sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.” He knew about that way, and he wanted to hear it.
“Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself.” Agrippa comes from the family of Herod: the same race of people, the same kinsmen, the same clan.
You said your sister thought you were going crazy. I was reading Acts 26:24; this was funny. They thought Paul was going crazy, and Paul said, I'm not crazy, I know what I'm talking about.
Agrippa said, 'Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian': the way Paul was talking, he almost wanted to follow this man Jesus Christ. Agrippa and them were already admiring us.

That's why Paul said, "Avoid vain and foolish babbling, because they're going to increase unto ungodliness." These people came with rhetoric. That's why when y'all hear us online, I'll be saying, "Yo, shut up. You're just talking. You just say stupid stuff. We don't want to hear this no more." This is what they were dealing with.

That's why Paul said, "Even of your poets," your poets, in Acts chapter 17. A fool tried to tell me that there were white poets teaching the people. No, the Israelites were into poetry and the literature of the Greeks.
Isaiah 58 mentioned the fast. Let's see if Paul kept the fast. Christianity says in the New Testament that's done away with.

The reference by the fast gives Leviticus 23:27-29: the fast was on the tenth day of the seventh month. That is the day of atonement, in which the priest would offer sacrifices for us once a year. But once Christ died on that cross, Paul could do it without the sacrificing, because Christ was that sacrifice.

Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house in Rome and received all that came in unto him. This takes place under Nero. Nero burning Rome: they would burn CDs; it was called Nero, and that was the symbol they used, Rome on fire.

Now, Asia Minor is where Paul went to Corinth, he went to Thessalonica, Pamphylia, Philippi, Corinth. What was some of those other places he went to? Somebody help me out. Ephesus, thank you. That's what I forgot. Ephesus, Philippi, Colossae for the Colossians. Yeah, he went to Smyrna as well.

Who is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed? I have planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. Paul planted by teaching people about Christ and repentance; Apollos watered by teaching them further. The teacher is the one pouring water, and he cannot pour too much or the seed corrupts.
Paul is writing to the church of God at Corinth and to all the saints in Achaia -- our forefathers, going over the very things we are dealing with.

note.label: When the Cup Becomes a Chain: Drunk in Bondage

points: Paul was not taught Christ from the disciples and was not awakened by them. Paul was literally awakened and taught by Christ himself.
Paul's credentials were astounding, above any other person. The things revealed to him were not revealed to many.
There were mysteries revealed to him on a level beyond the other disciples. Paul was able to go to scriptures and history and show the correlation between the past and the present.

Christ himself stopped Paul in his tracks and revealed himself to him even after his death, because Paul played an extremely important role in the gospel. If you are of the elect, if you were commissioned to do a job from the beginning, no matter what point of life you are in, you are going to wake up and fulfill the scriptures.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

points: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus. To the who? To the saints which are at Ephesus.

“Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus”. Paul writes to the saints at Ephesus, in Turkey. Who are the saints? The Psalms say why Paul calls these people saints.

Our beloved brother Paul, according to the wisdom given unto him, hath written unto you. Wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ. Peter read all his epistles and did not let anything erroneous slide. If Paul wrote error it implicates Peter, James, and John, the last surviving disciple, and makes Christ a negligent Messiah who waited three thousand years to send someone to fix Paul.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: The Apostle Peter respected the Apostle Paul for the correction. Watch what he wrote about the Apostle Paul.

Even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you: he said Paul got wisdom. Now why would he assume Paul had wisdom? Because Paul corrected him when he was wrong.

“Even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”: Peter acknowledged that wisdom was given to Paul, that the spirit of Christ was residing in Paul. That is what wisdom is.
